piezas.titular: DigComp 3.0 arrived and the teachers’ framework was expected; a year later it is still a draft
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025, the European Commission put AI into the digital competence framework for citizens, and teachers asked when theirs would follow. The final version is not expected until spring 2027.
cuerpo: On 27 November 2025, in ChatGPT-IA-edu, someone shared [DigComp 3.0](https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/jrc-news-and-updates/european-commission-updates-its-digital-competence-framework-digcomp-2025-11-27_en), the new edition of the European digital competence framework, published that same day. It came with more than 500 learning outcomes and AI, generative AI included, spread across all its areas. Amid praise and doubts over whether it would be enough, the question that followed was a different one: when would DigCompEdu, the framework for teachers’ digital competence, in force since 2017, be updated? No date was known; the bet was on UNESCO’s Digital Learning Week.

The wait has been longer. The Commission launched the update of [DigCompEdu](https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/DigCompEdu_en) in May 2026, as [the paper reported on 31 October](pieza:2026-10-30/digcompedu), and according to the Joint Research Centre (JRC) the final version is due in spring 2027. The draft keeps the six areas of competence, builds teachers’ AI literacy into the whole framework and asks them to understand how these systems produce their results and where they can fail.
A year on, then, citizens have their framework with AI and teachers are still working with one that predates ChatGPT, while its replacement is being revised.

fuentes.titulo: European Commission updates its Digital Competence Framework (DigComp) (Joint Research Centre, 27 November 2025)

piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diptych. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: the “DigComp” document with a tick and the “DigCompEdu” document with a question mark. On the right, “Today”: the first still has its tick and the second, “Draft”, is a document with a dashed border and a pencil.
repaso: «Nadie tenía fecha» pasa a «No se conocía fecha» (el mensaje dice «que yo sepa no tiene fecha»).
piezas.comprobado: Mensajes de la entrada del 27-11-2025 (ChatGPT-IA-edu): #42898 (DigComp 3.0 publicado, IA importante), #42905 (pregunta por la actualización de DigCompEdu, comprobado en t.me/ChatGPTedu/42905), #42906 y #42908 (sin fecha; hipótesis de la Digital Learning Week), #42899 (duda de si bastaría). Sin nombres de personas. Noticia del JRC (abierta el 21-11-2026): publicada el 27-11-2025, más de 500 resultados de aprendizaje, IA incluida la generativa integrada en todas las áreas. Página del JRC sobre DigCompEdu (abierta el 21-11-2026 y confirmada por búsqueda): actualización lanzada en mayo de 2026, versión final prevista para la primavera de 2027, seis áreas, alfabetización en IA integrada en todo el marco, entender cómo producen resultados los sistemas y dónde fallan, original de 2017; es un borrador. Enlace pieza:2026-10-30/digcompedu presente en publicado.txt y del mismo tema; el número salió el 31 de octubre. Tema distinto de los «Hace un año» del último mes (el del 12-11 trataba del marco AILit).
